utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. And good afternoon. May I remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence which still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Dorevska [Realtime transcript read in error "Mr. Stojanovski"].

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, I believe on Friday we left off where I was about to move to another topic. And I understand that it's your position, Ms. Dorevska, that in order for something to have authority in law, then it must be expressly stated in the legislation. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So if something is not expressly stated in the legislation, to put it another way, then there is no authority for it in law, as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Each obligation and task of the minister must be listed in the law in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. If I can ask you - I don't know if you still have your copy of the Law on Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can have the first Prosecution binder distributed at this point, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: While that is occurring we might mention at line 10 of the first page I'm -- I believe you actually correctly referred to Ms. Dorevska, but Mr. Stojanovski has come up as the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, if I can ask you, Ms. Dorevska, to please turn to tab 7 in that binder, and you'll find a copy of the Law on Internal Affairs, which, for the record is P86. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we can go to please ERN page N000-8965. That's in the English version. And if I can ask you to look at about the middle of the page where it says Article 13, Ms. Dorevska. Do you see that? Are you there?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, if we go to about the middle of the page we see that under the heading of directorate for security and counter-intelligence, there are a number of provisions. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And Article 13 specifically refers to or describes the activities that specifically relate to the security and counter-intelligence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And below that, we see that at the very end of Article 13, it says that the directorate is managed by a director, and that refers to the directorate for security and counter-intelligence clearly. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then we see that Article 14, which is the Article that you referred to in your examination-in-chief refers to the director, meaning the director for security and counter-intelligence, as being independent and carrying out the activities within the directorate and reporting to the minister and the government of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just to clarify matters, if you please can turn to the following page, we see that Article 17, which I believe you referred to in your examination-in-chief, which deals with the supervisory matters relating to the directorate and has the subheading of supervision over the work of the directorate, now that actually refers to, once again, the bureau of counter-intelligence. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the bureau for security and counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you would agree with me, Ms. Dorevska, that there is no corresponding provision in the Law on Internal Affairs which specifically refers to the bureau of public security in the same manner that we see here in respect of the bureau of counter-intelligence and security. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is so. However, the reason is that the law was passed in 1995 when the bureau for public security was not set up as a body within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And you've explained that in your examination-in-chief. But there's no provision here, for example, which clearly sets out for the bureau of the public security that, for instance, as it says in Article 17 that the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia is supervising the work of the bureau, is there, and that there's a committee that -- that takes -- that supervises that particular work, is there?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is so. However, the parliament does not supervise the bureau for public security even conditions such as these and in 2001, the parliament through the commission only supervises the work for public security, for security and counter-intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So in 2001, the parliament did not supervise the work of the bureau for public security, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no such provision because the parliament has a particular commission which supervises only the work of the bureau for security and counter-intelligence. There is no particular commission in the parliament which supervises the work for the bureau for public security, which does not mean that the parliament does not follow its work, however.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Wouldn't you have expected, Ms. Dorevska, that in 2001, that there have been an amendment, perhaps, to the Law on Internal Affairs and to include the public bureau of security expressly if it was in fact carrying out its work independently?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you that there should have been legal provisions and there were initiatives in that direction in drafting these provisions, regretfully, however, this was done somewhat later in about 2003 in the same manner as listed here, vis-a-vis the work of the bureau for public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So the provisions, as you just indicated, for the bureau of public security which state that the -- that it carries out its work independently and answers to the government and minister was done in -- actually in 2003?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not so. In 2003, amendments were made to the Law on Internal Affairs. However, in 2000, as I already said, the basic law was passed for organisation and work of the bodies of state administration, which set up the bureau for public security as a body within the ministry. In this manner, it established the independence of the director. I also that later in 2001, the rule book on organisation was passed which the independence of the director was clearly indicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, we'll get to the rule book in a moment, Ms. Dorevska. But if it was the intention of the drafters to deal with the independence of the director for the bureau of public security in the same way as the bureau for counter-intelligence, for example, wouldn't you have expected that an amendment would have been passed before 2003 to the Law on Internal Affairs, because as you indicated that was lexis specialis law, whereas the law on government and organisation of government bodies was a systemic law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so. However, as I said, there were attempts which pertained not to just this segment but to other as well. While the procedure for passing a law is more complex and lengthy due to these reasons, the manner of work of the bureau for public security was resolved in a different manner, through a by-law till the amendment of the law were passed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And have we seen this by-law, what by-law are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the rule book on the organisation and work of the ministry of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's go to that rule book. If I can ask you then to turn to tab 2 of your binder. Now where does it say in that rule book, Ms. Dorevska, that the director of the public security bureau carries out its duties independently?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, it only states here that the minister is the director while independence is listed in the organisation and work of the state administration. I believe this is Article 50 of the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And your referring to just for the record, the other law, the systemic law that you referred to before, which is the law on organisation and government bodies which would be P92. Is that what you're saying, just to make it clear?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so. I see the law and the rule book on organisation in correlation; I see them together.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But you would agree with me, that although -- that Article 50 of that other law refers to director of the ministry, it doesn't specifically deal with the public security bureau, does it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not so. It speaks of all directors in the bodies which are part of the ministry. This is a general provision which all persons who are directors in the bodies within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And why is it, Ms. Dorevska, that as you say, if attempts had been made to harmonize the law on internal affairs with this other systemic law, why was that -- why wasn't that done in 2001?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already explained that efforts were made to prepare this. However, there were many other provisions that needed to be amended in the law. Let me just say that this law from 1995 and still in force today and there are still some provisions which are not fully harmonised, however, we're intensively working on this harmonization.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that there might be gaps, then, in the law that are not entirely harmonised with the rules and regulations of the -- of the law on internal affairs or the other rules and regulations within the ministry. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps in certain case, yes, but the existence of a systemic law which solves the problem of the independence of the director in this case is sufficient, quite sufficient to provide him independence in his work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Except that there are no specific details with respect to the supervisory matters as to the director, is there? There are no provisions that deal with the supervisory matters of the director for public bureau of security, is there?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are provisions in the law on the organisation and work and in the law on government which point to the fact that supervision of the work of the ministry including the bodies within the ministry is carried out by the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But it also states that it's carried out by the minister, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the sense of supervision of work, of course the minister has the right to supervise over the work in that ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And if I can just move to another topic. Now if I can ask you, Ms. Dorevska, while we're on 1D107 to turn to the very last page, the organigram. And for the purposes of e-court, that would be 1D00-4415. Now this organigram shows that the OVRs were under the authority of the sectors or the SVRs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sections, the OVRs are organisational units which are part of the sectors for internal affairs, the SVRs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And they fall under the authority of the sectors, isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And above the sectors, in the chain of command would come the two heads of the police; the head of the uniformed police and the head of the crime police. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the -- which relates to operative work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can please then turn to 1D00-4414, we can turn to that page that is right -- right before the last page in 1D107. And above the head of the crime police and the head of the uniformed police is the director for public safety bureau. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If we look at the organigram, above that is the -- above the director for the public security bureau is the minister. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you mentioned in your testimony in your examination-in-chief, you explained that parts of the crime police and the uniformed police carry out the operative works, is that right, which are listed in Article 1 of the Law on Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you described them quite broadly, you said that these operative works are -- include the maintenance of public law and order, control road and traffic and crime police. You said it includes criminal procedure, prosecuting perpetrators of crime, everything that includes the operative tasks as part of the work of the ministry. Right.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the overall work of the ministry, but which -- work regarding the work of the bureau for public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So -- but what you're saying is that the operative work ultimately is headed by the bureau for public security. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The director for the bureau for public security is the first person who has oversight over the operative work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So all of these 9.000 persons that you described within the ministry, many of whom may be doing operative work, ultimately are answerable to the director of the public bureau of security. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not so. Each employee is responsible before his direct superior. That superior is answerable towards his direct superior and so it goes up the chain of command to the director.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So what you're saying is then the head of the OVR would be answerable to the head of the SVR, or the sector, is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And so, in turn, the head of the sector or SVR, may be answerable to the department for crime police or the department for uniformed police. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, this units have coordinative functions vis-a-vis the SVR, when we're talking about carrying out operative functions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But what I asked you is whether the head of the SVR, sector would be answerable to the head of the uniformed police or the head of the crime police?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Directly, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Didn't you say that the head of the SVR is normally answerable to or linked to the head of the -- the crime police and the head of the department for uniformed police?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not answer directly. There is coordination in action. If we're talking about the operative functions, of course, this is so. The department for crime police and uniformed police in this case have a function of coordination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are they answerable to the head of the crime police and the uniformed police indirectly then?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Then who does the head of the SVR answer to?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: More to the director of public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you're saying that the head of the SVR answers to -- answers directly to the head of the public security? I'm just trying to understand what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Answers to the director and they're connected to the department of uniformed police and crime police even with other organisational forms which are part of the bureau and which are under the direct authority of the minister, depending on the area that is in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And so the director is, as you told us at the outset of your testimony, is responsible or answerable to the minister. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can the director of public security, Ms. Dorevska, carry out operative tasks on his own?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can the director investigate a criminal matter, for example, or gather evidence or maybe even submit a report, a criminal report?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the director is an official and he coordinates the work within the bureau for public security. This is -- this is why there are so many other organisational units which carry out operative works. The role of the director is to coordinate the work and to reach decisions when certain coordinative activities are taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, suppose the director was -- becomes aware of a crime, say, for example, in the Bit Pazar police station. Can he then not file a report or instruct, perhaps, the head of the OVR to investigate the matter?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He cannot file a criminal report because there are operative employees which have to gather data and information and prepare the criminal report. If the director were to file criminal reports, then the operative employees would have nothing to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So are you saying then, Ms. Dorevska, that the director can never file a criminal report?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of a situation when the director could have or could have not filed a report, because I never dealt with operative functions. However, I believe that his role is to organise, coordinate and guide the work to indicate certain issues, while concrete supervisors and employees in organisational units carry out the work for which they have contracts.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, if I can then go to 65 ter 1155, please, in e-court. And if I can ask you, Ms. Dorevska, to please turn to tab 29 in your binder. Now, I'd like you to -- I can see that you're -- did you find that tab?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Could you please look at the first page.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I know you're flipping through the pages right now of the report and I'm just going to ask you if you wouldn't mind, if we can just do this slowly. If you can please look at the first page. It's a criminal charge, which is dated the 24th of July, 2001, and it's from the Ministry of Interior addressed to the public prosecutor. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it's a criminal charge against Ali Ahmeti. We can see that on the first page. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if you turn the next page. It also charges Veliu Fazli. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And on the third page and so on, we see that it's a charge against Gezim Ostreni. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, these are members of the NLA, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Could you turn to the page that is marked N001-0778. Now, you see this is a proposal to the basic public prosecution against the suspects to appear to -- to charge them for the stated criminal acts in this charge, and it's requesting a criminal procedure to follow against them. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if you can turn to the last page, please. Now this criminal charge was brought by Goran Mitevski who was then director of the public bureau of security, bureau of public security in 2001. Right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So it is possible, Ms. Dorevska, then, for the director of the bureau of public security to bring a criminal charge, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say expressly that the director cannot or must not file a report. From the document I can see I can only conclude this is a specific case, a large document and probably the services decided that it would be the best for the director of the bureau as the first among the operative officers to sign this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And isn't it because that this is actually a charge against members of the NLA leadership?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Have you never heard of members of the NLA leadership, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard, of course, of these individuals whose names I have read here in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you have heard of them in the context of them -- in the context of the NLA. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you know that this is a criminal charge brought against members of the NLA leadership, which is brought by Goran Mitevski, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't read this document so I can't know what is written within it. We're just speaking of it as a legal document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But you looked at the names of the -- of the persons who are suspects, who are charged. You said you recognised them and that they're members of the NLA leadership. You do know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them, of course, I've heard of, but I haven't read the document fully and I haven't read the contents of this criminal report or the reason why it was filed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Dorevska, you just mentioned a moment ago that you -- that the director would bring a charge like this because it's an important -- it was an important matter or a special matter, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just my conjecture. I really have no experience with regards to filing criminal reports or bringing charges and with regards to the operation of the bureau for public security from this aspect.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But you were the head of the legal sector, Ms. Dorevska, how can you not know when a director can bring a criminal charge?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The work of my sector is not related to the filing of criminal reports at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Wouldn't you be familiar as to the rules? I mean, you were just telling us about the operative matters and who can bring criminal charges and gather evidence.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But as a lawyer, of course, we do prepare or produce the acts but we have no junction point with the operative functions and the ways in which they are performed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Ms. Dorevska, given that the director was involved in such an important matter and brought this charge himself, wouldn't you expect that this is a matter that perhaps the minister would also be aware of?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say whether he was aware, because I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But you're not suggesting that the minister wouldn't be involved or at least aware of such an important charge being brought against members of the NLA leadership, are you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will say again: I don't know what was the communication and I don't know at all whether there were any reports sent to the minister and I can't either confirm or deny.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You mentioned a moment ago, Ms. Dorevska, that you don't know what charges or what operative matters that a director might be involved in. Wouldn't you give legal advice to directors? Wasn't that part of your function?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not part of my work at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you give legal advice to the minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the area that I cover.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So are there areas that perhaps a minister might be involved in that you may not know about?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There might have been such areas, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you suppose, Ms. Dorevska, that the minister would be concerned or would be involved in a matter that is -- that concerns the NLA leadership?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, are aware of what matters the minister might be involved in in relation to what you described as operative matters?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood your question well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you aware of what types of matters the minister might be involved in when it comes to operative matters?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not with regards to operative matters. But with regards to coordination and monitoring the affairs in the area of operative work, as a minister, actually, he has the duty to be informed of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you agree, then, that the minister would have a duty to be informed of matters that relate to operative tasks and to monitor and coordinate those tasks. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course the minister is a manager. He manages the ministry, and he surely needs to be informed by the directors and the other senior officers about the activities undertaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And why is it important to have the minister -- to inform the minister of these tasks?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since he is the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And a member --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: And member of the government, and of course he has the duty to inform the government about the matters in the area of internal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And as minister he is responsible for these issues, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what sense of responsibility are we speaking?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, you just said that he is the minister, he has to be informed of the -- of operative tasks. He is involved in monitoring and coordinating such tasks. He is responsible, ultimately, isn't he, as the minister.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Minister is a political figure and he has the political responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you're saying that as the political figure, he still has to involve himself in matters that are operative, because he represents the ministry and he manages the ministry. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not to perform the operative functions, just to receive information on what is going on in the area of operative work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, just a little while ago, Ms. Dorevska, you indicated that you didn't think that the director could be involved in performing the operative functions and yet we now see an example here with this criminal charge where the director was in fact involved with such a function. Isn't it possible that you just don't know whether the minister can be involved in operative functions?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the minister cannot and must not be involved in operative functions. He should be informed of the operative matters that the ministry is involved in.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Does the minister ever issue instructions based on the information that he receives?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of operative activities or in general, instructions related to the work of the ministry. What are you referring at?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: In terms of operative activities.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't have any involvement in that, and I have never seen any such type of instructions because, even if they existed, they do not arrive to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So it is possible, given that you just indicated you don't have any involvement for the minister to issue instructions in relation to operative functions, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no involvement and I do not think that the minister has issued any instructions in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But you're speculating now, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't speak of something that I'm not aware of.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But you are speculating when you say that you don't think that the minister could possibly be involved with such functions, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not speculating, I'm certain that the minister does not have any operative functions and must not perform operative works because he is a minister, he is a political figure and has a political responsibility. He represents the ministry. He is not an operative worker.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But can he not give instructions then to -- even if he doesn't perform operative work himself, can he give instructions to others to perform operative work?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of a legal document, yes, he can issue instructions, naturally.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So when you say in terms of a legal document, can he, for example, issue instructions to somebody to file a criminal charge against a -- a particular suspect or suspects?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The instruction is a legal document regulating particular matters that the law failed to regulate, so such document could not be issued by the minister. If you are referring to consultations with the director with the bureau for public security, if you're referring to that meaning of instructions, yes, of course, there are such consultations.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So it's possible then for the Minister to issue an instruction, say, to the director of public security, to file a criminal charge.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you pose the question it indicates the fact that the minister could order the director to file a criminal report. On the contrary, the director, or the individuals who are authorised for filing of criminal reports, file them whenever the prerequisites for that are met. The minister could not arrive at information with regards to any filing of criminal reports without receiving the data from the services, the staff that are working on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, assuming that the Minister arrives at this information because he receives it from the staff or he receives the information from any other way, could he then instruct the director to file a criminal report?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps he could talk to the director and establish or review all elements with regards to any filing of a criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And he could -- he could ask the director to file the report, can't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What if this related to a matter that was of great importance perhaps to the ministry? Can the minister not then request or ask the director to file a criminal charge or -- or have the members of the operative task staff investigate the matter?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are matters that are most probably discussed at collegiums in the more narrow circle when the directors and other responsible officers inform the minister about the situation in a given area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you saying that you are not aware of these matters, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I said these are collegiums in a more narrow circle. I have never attended any of those.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I see. So it is possible that at a collegium the minister may instruct a director to, for example, investigate a criminal matter that seems to be of importance to the ministry, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those would be conjecture. I could not give you an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I object to this manner of examination because the Prosecutor, at least on seven or eight occasions, asked the same question, having received an answer, and then is suggesting to the witness that the witness is speculating, so I don't think this kind of examination is in order and it surpasses the frameworks of what it should entail. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry Ms. Residovic, it's my impression that the Prosecutor is trying to get final and clear answers and the reasons for them from the witness and is -- when some of those answers were given, put to the witness that the answer was based on conjecture. So I don't see anything improper in what is being done in the cross-examination. Please carry on, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Dorevska, I'd like to you please turn to tab 44 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Actually, I may have to ask Madam Usher if she might distribute the second binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Dorevska, this is an investigator note of a meeting arranged by the Macedonian authorities in connection with the exhumation project proposed for a site near the town of Tetovo. Are you aware of that project?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we see here, according to this report, that the president of the country was present at the meeting, that Goran Mitevski, the director of the public security bureau was present at the meeting, and that Ljube Boskoski, then minister of the interior was present as well.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, not to go through the entirety of the document but there was a heated discussion at the meeting. And if I could ask you to turn to page 4, or the last page of that -- of this document, please. And if I can ask to you look at the second paragraph of page 4 which begins with the words: "He ordered," you see there that the president says to Mr. Boskoski, this is in reference to the president, that: "He ordered Mr. Boskoski to increase police patrols, to issue them armoured vehicles and body armour immediately and for them (police) to commence operations in the area tomorrow." And then he stated to Mr. Boskoski: "Mr. Minister, you will issue the police with all their powers now," and stated, "I am the president of this country and that is that." Ms. Dorevska, isn't the president in fact acknowledging the powers that Ljube Boskoski had over the police in that statement?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what document and what meeting is this about. I'm reading what you just stated. I can see the sentence and probably this is a strategic decision for the state.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But in that decision, he is acknowledging that the minister has power over the police to issue them with all their powers, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police has those powers, of course. In a meeting like this it won't be the head of the sector of internal affairs who would attend this meeting. The minister is part of the team. He received the order. I already said that the president's order entails an obligation for the minister. However, the minister, in order to carry out the obligation will undertake measures within the ministry and will communicate those to those who need to be the actual performers. As I can see, the director of the bureau for public security was also attending the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. But the president had addressed Mr. Boskoski, Ms. Dorevska, and my question was by saying to Mr. Boskoski that: You will issue the police with all their powers, he is acknowledging that Minister Boskoski has that authority to do so, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In terms of coordination and performing a task. Certainly following the hierarchy the president spoke to the minister and the minister is responsible for the situation in the area that the ministry covers. This does not mean that the minister will go to the field and issue -- give the powers directly to the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, if the public security bureau was independent, Ms. Dorevska, and the director was present, as you noted at this meeting, why didn't the president simply task the director with the -- that task, to issue the powers to the police?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the bureau for public security is part of the ministry and this is a body within the ministry. It is not an independent body, it is a part of ministry. And all the things that are taking place need to go through the ministry or actually through the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So even powers such as this and a matter of this importance would have to go through the minister. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course the minister needs to be informed when such strategic decisions are taken and the actual carrying out of the tasks will be transferred to those who are really in charge of performing the action.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it is the minister who would transfer those tasks to those who are in charge of performing the action. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not right, because these persons have original authorisations which they can carry out or implement.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that in this instance, Ms. Dorevska, that the president was merely informing Minister Boskoski of the strategic decisions?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this sentence, one can see that he gave the minister an order. However, an order for operative services to undertake necessary measures to that end, not the minister to transfer authorisations. The police officers have their authorisations.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So from this instance, we see that the minister can order the police to carry out their powers, as they're authorised, to carry out their operative tasks, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the minister has the right to issue orders. This is listed in the Law on the Organisation of work or bodies of state administration and the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And he has a right to issue orders in relation to matters that are set out in Article 1 of the Law on Internal Affairs, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps as a different manner of carrying out tasks, such as -- to undertake certain activities but not transfer of authority, as you put it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, we don't have to use the word "transfer of authority," I don't think I used that word. But he can order the police to carry out their tasks, and in this case, their operative tasks, can't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean directly to call a policeman in the field to tell him that he or she should do an operative task. Surely the minister does not do this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can he do it indirectly through the public bureau -- the director of the public bureau -- bureau of public security?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indirectly perhaps it is possible in a conversation with the director, and in undertaking certain measure for them to agree on the manner in which the activities will be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But, clearly, Ms. Dorevska, what we see here doesn't relate to a conversation, does it? It relates to instructions or orders, as an example.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that this document is not known to me. We're now talking about me -- about certain segments which you're pointing out to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What if the minister and the director disagree on a matter, Ms. Dorevska? Could the minister then instruct the director to instruct others to carry out a certain task?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is within the law and authorisation of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that would include matters such as matters that are listed, the operative tasks that you referred to earlier in your testimony, that are listed in Article 1 of the Law on Internal Affairs, couldn't they?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course the director and the minister are in communication. They talk to each other and they come to an agreement about the functioning of the ministry. The minister is responsible for the overall work before the government, and before the parliament, if you will.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But what if the minister and the director after they talk to each other, as you put it, disagree? Couldn't then the minister instruct the director to take a certain action that relates to operative tasks?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The director is a person who informs the minister whether the preconditions for undertaking certain measures have been fulfilled or not fulfilled. So if the director says that there are no conditions to that end, then the minister will have to respect this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But what if the director say there are conditions to that end but the director simply doesn't -- refuses to -- doesn't think that this particular operative task should be carried out and the minister disagrees with him? Doesn't the minister then have the last word?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is outside the legal provisions, then, of course, he would not have the last word. In my previous testimony I said that the ministry does not work according to the wish of the minister, but on the basis of law.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What if they are inside the legal provisions? Doesn't the minister have the last word?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He can suggest to the director that if all conditions are met, he can, in a conversation, point out that certain measures can be undertaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Isn't it true, Ms. Dorevska, that the minister can actually instruct the director to take certain measures, if he wished, because he is answerable to the minister? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Again, this is in the context of your previous question, and the answer I gave you that the wishes of the minister are not a command for the director.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But if it falls inside the law, it's not just the wishes of the minister, can't the minister instruct the director to carry out a certain task within the law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they will agree on what they need to take further on, if it's all within the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, if it's within the law and the minister disagrees with the director, isn't it true that the director then must do what the minister asks or instructs?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is the same question again, and I think my answer will be the same, the director and the minister must be coordinated: Director to inform the minister for conditions fulfilled and the minister in coordination with the director to decide about certain things.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But you haven't answered my question, Ms. Dorevska, because my question is, if the minister disagrees with the director on a matter that is within the law, can he not instruct the director to carry out that task?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it's a strategic decision in question for which the government previously elaborated and decided that it should be undertaken then the minister is obliged to do something and perhaps in this context he can give instructions, but, surely, under conditions when all pre-conditions are fulfilled.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, it's not -- what if it's not a strategic decision but it's a task that is within the law, say the Law on Internal Affairs. Can the minister not instruct the director to carry out that task? It's a simple question.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course he could.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am aware of the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We would normally go for another 15 minutes, if that's convenient; if it's not, say so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly not. I was mistaken because it was the afternoon session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now in your examination-in-chief, Ms. Dorevska, just moving on to another topic, you indicated that you saw several decisions, and some of them had been made by previous ministers and then there were perhaps amendments to those decisions or changes within those decisions, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, legal documents. They're basic documents and amendments which are passed by other ministers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So can one minister make changes to a decision made by a previous minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he can do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And can one minister then adopt the decision of the previous minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean when saying "then adopt."

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Let's just say there's a decision that a previous minister has made, isn't it possible for one minister to subsequently adopt that decision and carry out the tasks that the previous minister had decided ought to be made?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually these are concrete decisions for transfer of authorisations or other types of legal documents which a minister passes, and which the ensuing minister cannot change, because they don't pertain to concrete persons, but pertain to heads of units. But, again, here I'm not speaking about legal documents; that is to say, operative documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Can one minister cancel a decision made by a previous minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the decision in question. However, it does happen in practice. There have been such cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. If I can ask you, Ms. Dorevska, to please turn to tab 86, which is in the second binder. And that's 65 ter -- or, rather, Exhibit 1D112.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apologies, can you tell me again where -- what we should be looking at.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Tab 86, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, what we see here, Ms. Dorevska, is a decision dated 7 March 2001, if you look at the top of the date -- of the document. And it's a decision to form the headquarters of operative action Ramno. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that's a decision that was made by the previous minister, Dosta Dimovska. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that from the signature on the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So the previous minister under the laws had the power to create this operative action that was connected to the headquarters of the Ministry of Interior, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each minister can form a commission of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, it's not really referred to as a commission, is it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a decision for setting up a headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And if I can then ask you to go back to tab 22. And that's P381 for the record for e-court, and that is in your first binder, Ms. Dorevska. Actually, you can probably leave that document open.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps if I can ask Madam Usher to assist the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now do you see -- are you looking at P381, tab 22, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not looking at that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, if you look at that document, that's a document that also says decision to form the operative action Ramno, and it's signed by Minister Boskoski. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And we see that in this document, the composition of the persons who were assigned to this operation has been slightly changed, right? And this is P381, for the record.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in fact what Minister Boskoski has done is essentially changed the composition and placed Goran Mitevski as the head of the operation Ramno, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Doesn't that mean --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I see that my friend is on her feet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, your question is being formulated, so I think we can interfere at this point. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since the witness has already given the answer, it is the headquarters or staff of operative action, so it would be a good idea if the Prosecutor were to use the same permanent "operative action," and not operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That may or may not suit the line of questioning, but thank you for the suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Doesn't that mean, Ms. Dorevska, that Minister Boskoski accepted and approved this decision, or adopted it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister signed this decision, which means that he adopted this decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And then if we can --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll move on to another area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Dorevska, you've said at one point I believe in your testimony, in your examination-in-chief, that the minister can issue orders but only when there is an express authorisation granted by law or another regulation. And you said this at transcript page 9407, for the record. Now, if we go to P92, which is the law on the government bodies. I can tell you where it is momentarily. Tab 8 of the first binder, please. If you look at Article 55, Ms. Dorevska, just so that we're clear, there is no reference to the term "express." There is -- no express authorisation is required, according to this Article, is there?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, if you read the last part, it says: When he so authorised by law." The minister passes acts herein listed and other types of regulations when so authorised by law.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I see that. I just wanted to clarify that it doesn't say that there has to be an express authorisation by law, does it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This Article says just that, in order to issue an order, in a written form, or, in order to bring an instruction, plan, or a rule book, there must be an expressed authorisation by law.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But the word "express," is not there, is it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But authorisation established by law.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But you haven't answered my question. The word "express" is not there, is it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word "express" is not there. But the last part of the sentence clearly indicates that this must be expressly list in the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am aware of the time, and I think it might be a convenient moment at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have the adjournment now and continue at a quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, in your examination-in-chief, we -- you looked at -- you referred to Article 6 of the Law on Internal Affairs. And if I can ask -- perhaps we can go to that. It's at tab 7 in the first binder that I gave you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, in Article 6, as you can see, second paragraph refers to an employee that must -- of the ministry must implement the orders of the minister or the person authorised by him in connection with the functions of the ministry. Right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, aren't the affairs or the listed -- the affairs that are listed in Article 1 of the Law on Internal Affairs considered to be part of the functions of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. They are considered to be part of the functions of the ministry. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Part of the functions of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And would you agree with me, Ms. Dorevska, that if a superior gives an order and that order is followed or implemented, then that's an indication of his authority over the persons he gave the order to.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The persons have the duty to follow the orders. That is clearly indicated in the Article and this Article pertains to the duties of the employees.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. I appreciate that. But my question to you is if a superior gives an order and that order is followed, then that is an indication of the superior's authority over the persons he gave an order to, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those -- that authority belongs to his superior officer and if a person acting upon an order of the minister, as you say in this case, fails to perform the order, the direct superior has the duty to take measures under that -- against such person.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But that's not what I'm asking you, Ms. Dorevska. What I'm asking you is, just in general terms, if a superior gives an order to an individual, to a person, isn't that an indication of his authority over that person?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The person has the duty to follow the order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And would you agree, Ms. Dorevska, that if a superior didn't think that the order would be obeyed, that he wouldn't issue that order?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course the superior expects that the order would be obeyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And would you agree that if a person receives an order and obeys that order, it's because that person believed he a duty to follow the order?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They have the duty, unless, as it is written in the Article here, unless the following of the order would constitute a crime.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. In 2001, Ms. Dorevska, were you aware whether Minister Boskoski checked the laws and regulations every time he issued an order?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he did check. At any rate, the persons around him had the duty to indicate what the legal aspects were when issuing any order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you're saying that persons around him which would include perhaps yourself as one of the legal advisors, would have the duty to indicate to him what the aspects were? He would check with persons around him before he issued an order?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they have the duty to do so. If the minister asked me to prepare an order by which the employees will be prohibited travel abroad over a certain period of time, I have the duty to indicate that there is or there is no legal basis, ground for that. That is my duty as a senior officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you suppose that the minister in that stressful time, that stressful time during the crisis in 2001, Ms. Dorevska, was thinking about checking with his advisors about every order that he was to make and the black letter law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he did check.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what makes you say that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since nobody wishes to work in contravention to laws and regulations.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you know that he checked?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm just surmising. He did check when working on issues in my area. I can't say with certainty about other areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when you say issues in your area, you're referring specifically to issues of drafting laws, for example, or personnel issues, things of that nature, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes. With regards to the rights and duties of the employees and the personnel matters, of course also in the area of regulations since there were also laws that had been adopted precisely at that period of time that we had drafted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So issues that are outside of that area, you wouldn't know whether he checked or whether he was following the black letter law, would you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of operative work, I said I have no experience there. I have not attended those collegiums, but I believe that this had been done as the law and the constitution provide and that the director of the bureau for public security always informed the minister about the legislation in a given area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You say that you believe that this had been done. Are you, once again, just surmising?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I believed that it had been done, because whenever my area was the issue at stake he did confer with me and I suppose that he did that as well in the area of greatest importance for the work of the ministry, especially areas such as operative work and undertaking certain police actions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that area, as you say, is considered to be one of the greatest importance for the ministry, the operative work and the undertaking of certain actions?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the activities of the ministry are done through the two bodies between the ministry, the public security and the state security. This is also prescribed by the laws.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if -- and suppose I told you, Ms. Dorevska, that Minister Boskoski issued an order to the head of the uniformed police, Risto Galevski, ordering him to stop the police units, the special police units from continuing their combat activities in Aracinovo. Would that be an order that was within the competencies of the minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about any such order, and I could not comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is whether that would be an order that is within the competencies of the minister.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the legal aspect, that the minister is able to issue orders, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So the minister has the authority to issue orders for the cessation of combat activities, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is a political decision and strategy of the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, he, nevertheless, has the power to issue that order. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw already that the law provides that the minister has the authority to issue order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you account for the possibility, Ms. Dorevska, that Minister Boskoski in that complex time in 2001, that difficult, stressful environment, may simply forego the normal procedures and perhaps issue an order to a police unit on the ground?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Is that something you're -- is that, once again, something you're surmising?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I had nothing to do with the operative work and this is my opinion, that I do not think, from what I know of his manner and attitude of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. If I can ask you then, to, please, turn to 1D44, tab 9 in your binder, please. Now we have seen this document before, Ms. Dorevska. And if I can refer you firstly to the last two paragraphs of the document. And that deals with the -- with the command over the special tasks unit for the Tigers, and what it says is: "During the past period, the special tasks unit or certain parts of it were engaged for various types of tasks for which the orders and the requests come in an oral form from more leading workers at the MOI. "For the purpose of maintaining the hierarchy and the chain of command in the future for eventual engaging of the unit or parts of it, our request is necessary in written form to be submitted to the minister or the head of the department for police." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And this is a letter, or document, that is signed by the commander, by then commander of the Tiger unit, Captain Goran Zdravkovski, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention then to the date of the document, 19 July 2001, at the very top in the left-hand corner. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if you look at the top right-hand corner, there's a handwritten note signed by Ljube Boskoski, dated 20 July 2001, the next day. And what it says is: "I agree with your proposition that it should be requested in writing, but the minister approves alternative oral order from the minister in emergency situations." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So Minister Boskoski was indicating that the procedures provided for in the rules and regulations could be varied, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really did not understand the question or there was something wrong with the interpretation. I apologise for this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I'll repeat my question. Minister Boskoski was indicating that the procedures provided for in the rules might be changed or varied, that there is some flexibility in emergency situations, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing this indicates is that the minister agrees with what Mr. Zdravkovski offered in his letter, and this is during the period when the special tasks unit was under the competence of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, I appreciate that. But I think this indicates a lot more than what you've just said, doesn't it? Because he is saying that the minister approves that: "I agree with the proposition that normally a written request should be taken, or should be made, but the minister approves that an alternative oral order from the minister can take place in emergency situations." Isn't that what he's saying?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But why couldn't he issue an oral order in emergency situations? This is only normal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So it would be -- there is some room then for some flexibility and doing things a little differently outside the normal times in emergency situations, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only when the situation is out of the ordinary. There is such a possibility in other situations because of the urgency of the matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And particularly in 2001, when there was a greater -- there was a greater need for flexibility because of the urgency of the situation it would be normal for Minister Boskoski to react in the way that he did. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, he had the authority to do it since he had the direct superiority of approving deployment of the special tasks unit. Whether this would be done in writing or orally in emergency situations is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And he also had the flexibility to do it, didn't he, as the minister.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And just staying with the same document for a moment, if I can draw your attention, Ms. Dorevska, to perhaps the second paragraph in that document it says: Because the minister has assigned certain authority to the head of the department for police, the commander of the ESZ, which is the Tiger unit, receives orders and tasks also from the head. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So the minister can decide how much authority he wishes to assign to the head of the uniformed police and how much authority he wishes to retain. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever the minister has the source authority and in this case he does have it, he can decide to transfer that to -- to delegate that to another person. And if you look into the rule book on organisation, which speaks of the competence of the minister over the special tasks force or unit, there is a chapter that says in that certain situations, trainings and drills, the special tasks unit is under the competence of the head of police. This means that there has been a link here and it is not randomly that the minister transferred this right or part of his authority, I can't really say how big a part of his authority, to the head for police.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Just picking up from your point, you said: In certain situations such as training or drills, this document refers to a little more than training and drills, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I only wished to indicate what the functional links and the logics of delegating authority were, delegating to the head of the police department.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned, Ms. Dorevska, earlier that the minister held collegiums with his closest advisors, including Goran Mitevski, perhaps Risto Galevski, and others, and that the purpose of that was to help keep him informed of matters that were -- current matters that were happening or that would impact on the ministry. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister, pursuant to the rule book on organisation, organises or convenes collegiums in a broader or more narrow composition. I myself have been in attendance at collegiums in a broader composition and I know that there have been others in a more narrow circle. And this is a way for the minister to learn about the situation in the ministry. How else would he learn than through collegiums with people at responsible positions with the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And he would hold these collegiums and determine whether he wishes to have a broader or a more narrow collegium in order to keep informed of matters that are within the ministry, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And you explained that it is within this context that the director or the head of the bureau of public security may report to the minister about matters that are occurring within the context within the ministry, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. That is his duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the director of the bureau for public security would receive his information from his subordinates, such as Risto Galevski, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the head of the uniformed police, such as Risto Galevski, may receive that information from the sectors below them, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And they, in turn, would report that information up the chain of command. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And depending on what the information related to, once it's reported to the minister, the minister may make decisions about the work of the ministry. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister, together with the members of his collegium, and, if necessary, with the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And wouldn't the minister sometimes issue instructions or taskings to, say, the director for the bureau of public security?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I did not understand your question correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps that might be my fault. Wouldn't the minister, based on the information that he is getting at the collegium, perhaps make decisions and issue taskings to, for example, the director of the bureau of public security?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. On the basis of the analysis that has been made and what has been agreed on the meeting and within the framework, authorisation of the director, and all of this within the framework of the laws and the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And wouldn't the minister have the last word, as to what those taskings might be?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this can only be the result of the analysis of the overall situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And ultimately, the result of the overall analysis of the situation would end up with the minister. In other words, the minister would ultimately decide after analysis of the situation, as to the taskings that must be realised based on the information and the analysis that he receives?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that where tasks are concerned, people who are responsible for this will tell him about this, if all of this as a decision has been reached previously. The minister cannot know what needs to be taken on the ground. Can he hear about and analyse the overall situation and, in accordance with the regulations to agree or not to agree to what has been offered.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And once he hears about and analyses the situation, if he disagrees with a suggestion that was made perhaps by one of the members of the collegium, he can ultimately make that decision, can't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
