utterances.text: If he assesses that this is a strategically wrong decision and outside what the government does.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'd like you to turn to tab 25 of the first binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And this is Exhibit 1D184 for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, you see here, Ms. Dorevska, and you can see it on your screen as well, that this is a report from the meeting between the minister of interior affairs, Ljube Boskoski, and the head of the public safety bureau, Goran Mitevski, with Ambassador Daniel Speckhard who was the assistant secretary-general of NATO, and it is dated 5 September 2001. And we see here, you could look at the first page, that the minister has some information about the manning of check-points which Mr. Speckhard pointed out includes reservists and members of the Tiger unit. And if you look at the very bottom of this report, the third paragraph from the bottom, it says that Minister Boskoski expressed the following with respect to what had been said, that there are members of the reserve composition of the police at the check-points but not members of the Tiger units and the PEP. Now, Ms. Dorevska, wouldn't the minister have received that information from down the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not know. This is a report of minutes of a meeting, what has been said on that meeting, as to how he obtained the information, I could not give you my comment on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, how else would he obtain information about who is manning the check-points?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Surely someone must have given him that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that information would have come from -- come up -- come from up the chain of command from the police forces on the ground, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then we see here, Ms. Dorevska, that the minister made a decision. And if you look at the very bottom of this report on the first page, it says: "Precisely because of the big number of disinformation which are acknowledged about the behaviour of the police, Minister Boskoski agreed that there be a NATO representative who will be present at the check-points at all times and who will have a clear picture of the situation at the check-points." And then it says: "Based on the acceptance of the idea that NATO is present at the check-points in the country for placing technical equipment, for registering the entire situation and for conducting of the procedure for fast realisation, Minister Boskoski assigned the head of the public safety bureau, Goran Mitevski, and General Aleksander Doncev to be directly involved in the realisation." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So Minister Boskoski made a decision and assigned the director of the bureau for public safety regarding the manning of the check-points. Basically he ordered Goran Mitevski to be in charge of this task, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In any event, I see this as a way that the director and General Doncev be directly involved. That is to say, that they should follow the situation directly and inform the minister so as the minister could obtain proper information about the state of affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, the decision is that NATO or members of NATO is present at the check-points, and it later then says that Minister Boskoski is assigned or Minister Boskoski assigned Goran Mitevski and General Aleksander Doncev to be involved in a realisation of this task. It's a little more than remaining -- keeping informed of the situation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand this as a situation where these persons are directly authorised to be involved in the realisation so that the minister can receive information directly from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And he assigned them this task in order for him -- so that he can continue monitoring the situation. Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister does not carry out this kind of monitoring. He has to have all the information in regards to certain activities of broader scale.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, is the subject of police check-points or the manning of police check-points and who is deployed at those check-points, is that expressly described in -- as one of the competencies of the minister in the law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Deployment of people -- the obligation of the minister in this regard is to pass decisions for deployment of persons in specific work tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that would include the manning of check-points?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Persons who are directly in charge in the ground -- on the ground will decide on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But in this case, Minister Boskoski agreed that certain persons are to be present at check-points, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But most probably in terms of their number and the need of certain persons being there, not in terms of concrete individuals with concrete names.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So what you're telling us is that Minister Boskoski can make decisions as to the number of personnel and other decisions of that nature, that impact on matters that are on the ground?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there's a need to deploy persons from one to another organisational unit or police officers from one to another police station, the decision for deployment as a final decision is passed by the minister of the interior with his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But is the manning of check-points considered to be an existing work post or job position, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And doesn't the collective agreement that you had talked about before specifically refer to the deployment of individuals to job positions, to different job positions within an organisational unit?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It speaks of deployment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So that kind of deployment is different from this deployment, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Ms. Dorevska, I'd like you to please turn to tab 37. And that is P468. Now you see here, Ms. Dorevska, this is a document --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honour, I believe there might be a technical problem. I'm not getting the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, I've only heard you speaking in English for a little while. If there was anything being spoken in another language, it has been not translated. But what do you think is missing?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm sorry I actually heard the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There was just an interference in another language. It's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, if we can then have a look at this document. It's a telegram from the cabinet of the minister which is dated June -- 11 June 2001, signed by Ljube Boskoski to the sector Kocani, addressed to the sector Kocani. And it says that: "In order to undertake security measures in the territory of the Republic of Macedonia and the replacement of police forces it is needed that on the 12th of June, 2001, 50 policemen and their senior officer in charge be transferred to the military barracks," and it has the name of the barracks in Kumanovo, "driven in your vehicles." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, as I understand it, Ms. Dorevska, you explained in your testimony that when there is an order issued by the minister, or a decision, that always at the top of the document, the legal grounds or the basis for that order is marked. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now we don't see any reference to the legal grounds or basis for this order, is there?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But this is a simple telegram.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So the minister can actually issue an order by way of a telegram and he doesn't have to issue an order following the formality of the procedures that you described before. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We don't have an order here. At least I don't see anywhere on the text of the document where the minister says, "I order that 50 police officers be transferred." In this case, the minister informs three services that 50 police officers should be transferred, and I see this within the context of his right to deployment and the decision which was previously passed by the bureau for public security.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, if it's not an order, Ms. Dorevska, then what else is it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, according to what I see, this is an analysis done previously and a decision passed previously, and this is a telegram, an information to the sector of internal affairs in Kocani which should undertake part of these obligations to the sector of finances and other common affairs, which have to provide the arms, the ammunitions, camouflage uniforms, and all else that falls under its responsibility and to the sector of analytics and research.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Why would the minister need to send out this information, Ms. Dorevska, if you're suggesting that it's not an order and it is merely something that was passed previously?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not an order at all. According to me, this should be signed by the director for public security, perhaps he was absent at that time, and it was signed by the minister of the interior, this means, carrying out a decision previously passed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If it is carrying out a decision that had been previously passed, then why would the minister need to send it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to inform the persons who need to carry out this order and to increase the importance of the obligation that needs to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, if he is informing the persons to carry out this order, then that makes it an order, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a legal sense, this is not an order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, in a practical sense is it an order?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a practical sense, it is an information about a previously passed decision, as I said, because there may be a need for these 50 police officers to receive deployment decisions. Therefore, the responsible persons will have to prepare a proposal and to state which 50 police officers are in question. Here the minister does not list the name of the persons. He just speaks of the need of transfer of 50 police officers. Surely he himself could not himself know the number of people who will be necessary to carry out a certain activity.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But in order for that activity to be carried out, for the 50 policemen to be transferred, it was necessary for the minister himself to -- to send out this order, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in that sense in which you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, then, why would he need to send out the order in the first place, Ms. Dorevska? If it was a previously passed decision and the commander of the -- of these policemen knew about this decision, why would the minister himself need to send this out?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had prepared this document, then I could give you a decisive answer on this question. However, we are speaking about a document prepared by someone else. I told you my opinion and my viewpoint on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But it plainly says, you would agree, Ms. Dorevska, that what the minister is saying that in order to undertake security measures in the area, replacement of police forces is necessary. And it plainly says that 50 policemen with their officer in charge, be transferred to the military barracks. That's what he's instructing, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct. It is written clearly and then the activity is so transferred to Mr. Sapalovski Mitko as it is written here. This is something given to a person which he has to carry out now, something which has previously been reached in the form of a decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in order for that decision to be carried out, the minister had to send out this instruction, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Looking at this document now, there's another matter which I have noted. The sector of finances, another common affairs was under the direct command of the minister. Perhaps this is the reason due to which the minister signed this document, because the director of the bureau for public security could not issue such a request to the sector of finance, because he was not authorised to do so. Since we have three organisational units in question here, I can see the only logic in this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So without the Minister's involvement and his instruction to these sectors, is what you`re saying, then this order could not have passed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Surely it could be carried out, but with one document we have three organisational units which are differently positioned or encompassed in this way. And I believe it was felt this was the most efficient way to carry out what had been previously decided upon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: How do you know, Ms. Dorevska, that the decision was previously made? You've said that several times. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only assume because the minister cannot know the number of police officers that are necessary to be transferred from one to another work post.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you're assuming that on the basis of the information that the minister was given this information. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the basis of the document which I am reading.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You mentioned, Ms. Dorevska, that this order surely could be carried out but with one document you have three organisational units which are differently positioned or encompassed in this way, and the minister has the authority to direct these organisational units, that, as you point out, are referred to at the top of this document, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In a way, this is not an order. You always are saying the same thing, that it is an order and I claim that it is not an order. It is merely information and this is not management in question. We are -- we can see at the top of the documents that the minister is expressing a need for the transfer of police officers to the sector of internal affairs Kocani. The second part pertains to finances which is also very important. And in this case only the minister can act on this, because no one else can indicate anything to this sector.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Without the minister's action then, is what you're saying, Ms. Dorevska, then this decision would not have been carried out, would it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it would have been carried out, but that it would have been necessary to have more documents and to have various people sign these documents: One by the director of the public security and one by the minister. I believe the assessment was with this one document it was most efficient and the best way to carry out this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you receive information of this nature, Ms. Dorevska, for example, that is stated in this document, when you received it from your superior, would you act on it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would act on it if it is within my authority to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, assuming it is within your authority to do so and your superior gave you what you refer to here as information, then you would act on it, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would act on it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You also mentioned several times that you felt -- you think that this is -- this telegram is perhaps the most efficient way of sending or carrying out the decision. Why was it necessary in 2001 to act most efficiently?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of the situation in which the country was found.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you're saying it was because of the complex security situation that things had to be done perhaps much more quickly, more rapidly and more flexibly?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can it be otherwise in a situation such as we had in 2001?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to another topic. Ms. Dorevska, you mentioned that, and obviously you knew Minister Boskoski, you worked with him for some time, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not for a very long period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But, nevertheless, you did work for him. He was your superior, was he not?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did Minister Boskoski know what his obligations and responsibilities were as minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he did know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did he understand what his duties and obligations were, what his authority was within the hierarchy or the chain of command within the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is a rather personal question that would deal with Mr. Boskoski, to what extent he did or did not know about certain issues. I couldn't really answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Dorevska, you have been telling us several times throughout your testimony that you didn't think Minister Boskoski would do certain -- would take certain actions or would do certain things. So it appears that you -- you do know Minister Boskoski and his attitude and his -- his understanding of what his duties are. Don't you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right. I did mention this, but I connected it with my work, and I know how he acted with regards to the matters that were within the remit of my sector. He would ask whether something is viable or not whether something can be done or it is something that cannot be done and from this, I can draw the conclusion that he acted in the same way with the heads of the other departments.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you're saying that you don't know what Minister Boskoski, what activities and what -- what he's done outside of the remits of your sector, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The things I haven't seen or heard, with regards to those, I can't deny or otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did Minister Boskoski understand how much power and authority he had to issue tasks to people within the ministry, as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the word "power," "mokj," is a rather broad notion. Mr. Boskoski knew what his duties were with regards to the employees and the exercise of their rights.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like you to turn to tab 26 in the binder, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's Exhibit 402, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you know, Ms. Dorevska, that Minister Boskoski wrote a book titled My Battle for Macedonia regarding his activities and the conflict in 2001?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Have you read this book?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like you to turn to page 12, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And that is, for e-court purposes, N000-9618. I think that's the Macedonian version, N000-9618.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you have that there?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is most probably it. Page 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Page 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps if I can just ask Madam Registrar to assist to find the page. It`s the page that corresponds to N000-9618 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll just read it out. From the bottom of page 12, Minister Boskoski writes --

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but it reads here page 20. I can't really follow what you're reading.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just to add to your troubles, none of the Judges have any of these pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, I apologise for that, Your Honours. I thought those pages would make it into the binder. Apparently they haven't. But hopefully we'll try and find them on e-court momentarily. If I might have the Court's indulgence for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would it be practical to have a break now and you can find the pages and sort out the issue during the break?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, perhaps that would be best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will do that and we will resume at five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you for the indulgence, Your Honours. Your Honours, if I might just begin by distributing the English versions of P402 to Your Honours so that you now have it to add to your binders. I apologise that it wasn't in there to begin with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: That's what we needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Dorevska, I'd like to you to turn to your page number N000-9618, and in the hard copy it would be page 12 -- rather, page 20. And in the English version, it's page 12. Now, this is how Minister Boskoski, and I'd like you to draw your attention to the paragraph begins with: "From the manager post in the office for security and counter-intelligence." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't see it here. It is N000-9618 is the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at page 20 specifically, Ms. Dorevska.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is now page 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And do you see the paragraph that begins: "From the manager post in the office for security and counter-intelligence."

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. And that says: "From the manager post in the office for security and counter-intelligence, I was promoted to the state secretary at the Ministry of Interior. In that position, in the strictly established police hierarchy, the obligations and responsibilities were also bigger. The state escalated and the circumstances led to a government reconstruction, where I was appointed minister of interior." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then he continues, and he says: "The prime minister, who, on several occasions publicly demanded a proclamation of a state of martial law in the country in order to quickly, efficiently and professionally put an end to the intruders, to which demand the president of the country did not react, wanted a more sophisticated action in that situation by the Macedonian security forces, which greatly depended on the MOI top management." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Wasn't the structure in the ministry exactly how Minister Boskoski described it there, that there was a strict hierarchy within the ministry and with the minister on the top of that hierarchy, and that the action by Macedonian security forces depended on the MOI top management?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. As a political figure and as someone who needs to bring a strategic decision with regards -- or in accordance with the government's position.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like you to then turn to your version of -- N000-9652 in the Macedonian version, page 88; and in the English version, it's page 41 in the hard copy. And the ERN number for the English is 9647. Now, I draw your attention to about the middle of the page where the paragraph begins with: "The talks were open and it was possible to speak of all the problems faced by the citizens." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in about the middle of that paragraph it says: "I agreed to meet them because I knew very well the problems they had and their fierce pain, both in the soul and in heart. Being the minister of defence," and I think that is an incorrect interpretation, should say the minister of the interior, "I promised that the Macedonian security forces would do all they're authorised to expel the terrorists from the occupied villages or eliminate them." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So Minister Boskoski saw himself as having sufficient power to do everything in order -- to do everything he could to instruct or task the security forces to expel the terrorists from the occupied villages. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reads here precisely, everything within their power or within their competences. This means everything within their competences and the law, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, then I'd ask you to turn to N000-9644, page 72 in the Macedonian version; and N000-9641, page 35 in the English version. And if you look at the very bottom --

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I see only the English version. Page 72, yes, it's fine now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you look at the very bottom of that page, Ms. Dorevska, starting with the paragraph of: "I assure you there will be no truce with terrorists." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And about the middle of that page it says: "Being the head of the Ministry of Interior, I can guarantee the future of the state." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't find it. Is it on the same page, on page 72?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I believe it is, Ms. Dorevska. It should be in the middle of the paragraph that begins: "I assure you will there will be no truce with terrorists." Do you see it now?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, now I see it. It is in another page.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. So it says: "Being the head of the Ministry of Interior, I can guarantee the future of the state." Is that how much power Minister Boskoski saw, or believed he had, as far as you were aware?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that he thought he had the -- so great a power. I believe that he said that he would invest all efforts to resolve the situation in the state.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, at the outset of your testimony you said that you didn't believe that Minister Boskoski went out in the field. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said it, but maybe he went to the field to support the people who were there. It is his duty to see where the police officers are, to see whether they feel any needs and to also give them moral support.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, as minister of the interior who is -- who is, as you say, following the law and -- and making decisions and taking activities within his authority, is going out into the field with police during the course of police operations or battles within the competencies of his -- his competencies as minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say at all that I was aware of a situation where the minister went to the field to participate in a police action. I said it is possible that he had gone to field where police officers were stationed during some period of time, to give them moral support, taking care about their rights and obligations. Maybe they had certain needs that they wanted to state to the minister. So within the scope of his competencies he would work on improving the conditions of these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how -- why is it then at the very outset you said that you believed he wouldn't have gone out or he didn't go out into the field?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me whether he went into the field in terms of police action, and I believe that the minister never participated in a police action, this minister nor any other minister. But to go to the field, to visit the people, that he is in a way the senior officer, I believe that he has done that and I don't think that would be illegal.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And where does say in the law, in the black letter law that can he go out into the field?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise, but there seems to be an error in line 21. Because he said that he never participated in police stations whereas the -- what the witness said is in police action, actions. So it should be actions, not station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps I can just repeat my question, Ms. Dorevska. Where does it say in the black letter law that the minister can go out into the field?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The black letter law never states that the minister can go to the field but when we're speaking to the field we're referring to a broader sense of that term. If a situation takes place or if a police action takes place or there is an action where police officers are wounded or have been killed, it is the moral duty of the minister to go visit them, to see if there is any need to take certain action with regards to their rights.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, where does the law say that, that it is the moral duty of the minister to go out and visit persons in the field to determine whether they -- he can take certain actions with regards to their rights?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my experience, I don't remember reading in a law ever a provision speaking about the moral duties of a person.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you suggesting then, Ms. Dorevska, that Minister Boskoski, if he feels he has moral duty to take a certain action, then he simply can do so with respect to matters that relate to the ministry without it being expressly stated in the black letter law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is a moral obligation and the rights of the people that he is superior of, then certainly, yes. I'm not referring to the Minister Boskoski only. I'm speaking about any minister. If such huge situation takes place, or police actions, as they are carried even now, it is the obligation, moral obligation of the minister to go and see what is happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What other kinds of obligations are there that are not covered by the law, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know such obligations. I'm speaking from a moral standpoint.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, what kind of moral obligations exist that wouldn't be covered by the black letter law that the minister can -- can do or can take decisions regarding.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about such obligations, but I do know that the minister is morally responsible to visit the persons he heads at the time when people of security forces are being killed and when persons -- and these people may have certain needs regarding their rights within the ministry and when, for a long time, they're at a given period or a given place on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, although what you're saying is not in the law, is it? You believe that he has the right, the moral obligation to go out and visit people in the field, although that is not the law, is it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe when people resign due to moral reasons this is not expressly stated in the law, but they feel that they will take on their responsibility in this way, by undertaking the step of moral responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So can the minister determine what moral responsibility or obligation he has and take a decision or perhaps issue an order as a result of that moral responsibility?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister can go and visit police officers and the police officers can give their comments about their engagement. Perhaps they require additional food or they have other rights that need to be met and this is an obligation on the part of the minister and then to try to improve the conditions in which these people are in, but we must differentiate between morality and obligation provided for by law, and I think this is a very clear situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But do all ministers have the same beliefs or the same -- what they view as their moral obligations?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe all ministers, and I have worked with five ministers up until now, there have been various situations and there has always been this type of visits in circumstances which entailed larger events.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, apart from the visits, what other moral obligations would a minister have that would not be described in the law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A visit in itself is not a moral obligation. A moral obligation of the minister is to see what is happening with his people on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And what other kinds of things can a minister do that are not described in the law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He can only do what is prescribed by law.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But you just told us he can go out into the field and give moral support and find out if his troops need more food, et cetera, and that's his moral obligation which is not described in the law. So I'm asking you what other types of things can he do that are not described in the law?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to this morality aspect which I'm speaking about, I don't know of anything else. Do you think that the minister would sit in his office and follow events on television? Of course, under certain circumstances morality leads him to go and see what is happening with the police officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And morality may lead him to make certain decisions and perhaps be a little more flexible than what is written in the black letter law. Right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And Minister Boskoski, as you just pointed out, didn't just sit in his office and watch television, did he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, and I cannot respond to this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. So you`re saying you're not aware of his activities?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like you to turn to page 23 in the English version; page 46 in the Macedonian; N000-9631 of P402. Now, if I can ask you, Ms. Dorevska, to look at the paragraph that begins with the words: "I immediately set off for Tetovo." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it says: "I immediately set off for Tetovo. I wanted to acquaint myself with the situation on the very spot. This became a regular practice for me, because I am a man who wants to observe the situation up close, and the security situation in the Republic of Macedonia at that time demanded that I be always with the Macedonian defenders in the field, that is, in the immediate focus of events. There where the hoots of bullets next to your own ears is a reality." And then he talks about visiting Tetovo and in the following days: "I visited the Lipkovo area. I was informed on the spot about everything that was going on in the field." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Doesn't that mean that Minister Boskoski was going out into the field on a regular basis and getting his information outside of the collegiums that you had described earlier?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are sentences of a book which reflect a situation at a given period of time, and I am expected to interpret them as legal documents. However, there is one sentence which states: "I was informed on the spot about the situation." I think that is a self-explanatory sentence. As for the whole paragraph, I will give you my same response. Why the minister should not go in the ground where many police officers are located and to see what the situation is with those people which he manages and leads.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: You didn't really answer my question. When you say sentences -- these are sentences of a book which reflects a situation in a given period of time. You have to interpret them as legal documents. I mean, this was a book written by Minister Boskoski himself. Why do you have to interpret his book as a legal document?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I'm a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. But this isn't a legal document, is it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly why I made my comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Why would have you to interpret the book as a legal document? You're not an expert, are you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is exactly so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When you say this is exactly so, you agree that you're not an expert, are you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not an expert, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Dorevska, if I ask you, then, to look towards the bottom of that same paragraph and it says: "I came back there after a few days together with the manager of the public safety bureau, Goran Mitevski. I familiarised the press with the MOI measures for achieving the priority concern for the civilian population." And then he says: "The Macedonian army and police will establish the constitutional and legal system on every inch of the Macedonian land for which we shall do everything that is necessary." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Does that seem to you, Ms. Dorevska, the kind of minister who wanted a director to work on his tasks independently or was he the kind of minister that liked having control over the ministry and its activities?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The director of the bureau is independent in carrying out his tasks and this is the usual situation where the minister and the director go together to a place. Here journalists are also mentioned, and you know that statements about a certain situation are always given by the minister. He is accountable before the government, the journalist, and at the request of the parliament. How else can he obtain such information unless he visits the places where the police officers are located?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, didn't you earlier tell us, Ms. Dorevska, that he obtained his information at the collegiums through his advisors and the director through these meetings at the collegiums? Isn't that how you said that was how the minister would obtain his information?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. But for undertaking certain measures and from these sentences which I have read, this is not undertaking police measures on the ground but getting information about the -- the state of affairs, about the situation itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But you never mentioned earlier, Ms. Dorevska, that he went out into the field to get his information from police -- police operations or police persons on the ground, did you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not have mentioned it because I do not know. It is for the first time that I have read these sentences from the book. I am giving my comments in a way which I think logically derives from what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So your basically surmising or speculating on the basis of what you're reading in the book. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not speculating at all, but I'm making the difference between operative authorisations of the minister and visits of the minister on the ground to see people who are there for days, weeks months.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: When Minister Boskoski, Ms. Dorevska, gave statements on television, the people in the Ministry of Interior saw them -- saw him as their superior, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. He is their superior. He is the first man of the ministry. This is listed on -- in the law for the organisation and work of the bodies of the state administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And when Minister Boskoski went to the ground, to police operations on the ground, or the battles, do you think he simply absorbed information and gave no instructions?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about a situation such as this. I believe he spoke with the police officers from what I am able to read here and that he was acquainted of the situations they were facing and what they need.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But that wasn't the question I asked you. I asked you when Minister Boskoski went to the ground to police operations, to visit the police on the ground, do you think he simply absorbed information without giving any instructions?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot respond to this question at all, because I didn't know and I do not know what happened when the minister visited those places as it is written here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you respect Minister Boskoski, Ms. Dorevska?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Would you consider Minister Boskoski a responsible person, responsible minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Do you believe he was responsible in carrying out his duties?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And he carried them through.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did he always respect and follow the rules of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe you already asked me this question, and I told you that where my area is concerned, I cannot claim with certainty about other areas, but with my area, this was so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like you to turn 65 ter 1076. And in your binder, tab 41, please. Now, if you look at the very top of that document, this is Minister Boskoski's personnel or employment record with the ministry, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first page of a case file. Cover page.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And the cover page refers to Ljube Boskoski.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it comes from the sector for legal and personnel matters, your sector, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And I would ask you if you could turn - perhaps with the assistance of Madam Usher - to N006-6243. Now that's a decision that is signed by you. Is that right, Ms. Dorevska? It's a document that's signed by you?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it's dated the 20th of June, 2003.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it's addressed to Ljube Boskoski with an address, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it says that: "The decision that was brought by the Ministry of Interior with which you were rewarded with a fire-arm is annulled with this decision which is attached herein." Do you see that? I know you're looking through the other pages, Ms. Dorevska. I'm just asking if you could look at this one page first, please.

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's fine, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If you look at about the middle of the page it says: "Regarding the stated, you are called to return the mentioned award to the Ministry of Interior in the municipality of Kisela Voda to the check-point for weapons in the working hours ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then you say: "In case the award was alienated, you should pay for it in its monetary value." And it gives the -- a bank account number. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So you informed Minister Boskoski after he left the ministry to return the weapon that he had been awarded, right, as part of your duties?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Then if we turn to --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: If I can ask the assistance of Madam Usher once again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: To -- actually, I'll turn to the next page which is N006-6244. And that is the decision of annulment, isn't it? And in that -- right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in that decision it says that Ljube Boskoski is obligated to return the given award in a period of 15 days from the day of the decision, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And in the explanation below that it refers to Article 71 from the Law on Internal Affairs, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then, once again, it -- at the bottom of the document, it says that if -- if the award was alienated, then he is obliged to pay the monetary value for it, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And it's signed by Minister Hari Kostov, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And then if we turn to the following page, which is N006-6245, it's dated 21st of August, 2003. It's a delivery note, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: At the very bottom of the delivery note it says: "On 18 November, 2003, at 1700 hours, we met with Ljube Boskoski in front of the entrance of his house on Georgi Skrizevski Street, number 23D, and after the named person read the decision and comprehended its contents, he rejected to receive it, the decision, and to sign up the delivery note." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Then we see -- if you turn to N006-6250, or zero, I think you may be able to see it on your screen, you see that that is another delivery note that was dated 20th of August, 2003. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And, once again, it says that the person rejected the receipt of the decision, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And if I can then ask you to finally turn to N006-6242 --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps with the assistance of Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Now, this is a letter from a commander of the police station Centar, dated 25 November 2003, addressed to the Ministry of Interior, sector for legal and personnel matters, which is your sector, right? And it says that: "Attached to this file are the decisions concerning Ljube Boskoski from Skopje. And we would like to send back to you and would like to inform you that the named person, after reading these decisions refused to receive them and said the following, to send them back to the one who issued them to Hari Kostov." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So, Ms. Dorevska, when Minister Boskoski left the ministry, he was repeatedly asked to return the property of the ministry and he refused, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not property of the ministry. This was a monetary award and the minister, just as the other employees, received it on the basis on Article 71 of the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Nevertheless, it was decision requiring him, obligating him to return this monetary award after he left the ministry, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't see anything illogical in the fact that he rejected to sign the delivery note. The administrative procedure lists the overall procedure of how an act is delivered and the person has the right to reject to accept such a delivery note. Then it is stated how this document can be submitted in a different manner. What happened with the decision further on, I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, he didn't just reject to sign the delivery note, Ms. Dorevska, as we saw in that last document he said to send them back to the one who issued them, to Hari Kostov, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true. This is what is written.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So he refused to return the weapon that he was obligated to return, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had the obligation on the basis of the decision annulling this, but he received that pistol in a legal procedure and most probably his assessment was that what the minister that followed did was not proper.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: My question to you was that he refused to follow his obligations. He refused to return the weapon that he was obligated to return, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He refused to receive the decision annulling it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, do you know for a fact that he returned the weapon as he was required?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't confirm that fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And we just saw, Ms. Dorevska, that those decisions or the delivery notes were sent to him back in August, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this what is written here, then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, we just looked at that. We just looked at those documents, the delivery notes were sent to him in August, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the document I see here in front of me, I can see the date, 25th of November, 2003.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: That's the document, Ms. Dorevska, where the commander of the police station Centar is informing the Ministry of Interior that Ljube Boskoski refused to receive the decisions and to send them back to the one who issued them, to Hari Kostov, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw the document now, the receipt note and this is in August 2003.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So if he had agreed to return the weapons, Ms. Dorevska, why would it have been necessary for the commander of the police station Centar, two months later in November to inform the Ministry of Interior that Ljube Boskoski had not done so?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're speaking again about the same notice. He never received the decision. He refused to receive the decision. And the staff that were serving the decision through the legally prescribed legal procedure, they had the possibility to secure the service. Until someone has received the decision, they could not receive it in a legal way, they could not really follow the obligations that ensue from it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So by refusing to receive the decision, he was acting outside the law, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The law provides obligation -- provisions on how the decision can be served, in case the recipient refuses to receive it. Obviously the police station commander did not know how to do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you suggesting, Ms. Dorevska, that anyone in the ministry can simply refuse to receive a decision and then that they would not be obligated to follow that decision by the simple refusal of not receiving it?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you did not understand what I was saying. He has the right to refuse the signing of the decision but there is a procedure that then the services can follow and still serve the decision although it was refused. I can't see that this procedure was followed here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: According to the decision, however, Ms. Dorevska, he was obligated and did not have the right to refuse to return the weapon, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I repeated several times. He has the right to refuse to sign the decision if he disagrees with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And does he have the right to not return the weapon because he didn't sign the decision?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he has not been served the decision through the proper procedure, then there is nothing on the basis of which he should act.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Are you seriously suggesting, Ms. Dorevska, that he can simply circumvent the rules and the -- his obligations by a mere refusal of accepting a delivery note? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just wish to say that this is the usual procedure in the ministry, and in all ministries in general. That people simply do not want to sign the documents that they are served. However, there are mechanisms, legally prescribed that need to be followed and then the person is served the document as the law provides. From this, I can see that he refused to sign the decision, which means that he never received the decision. And then the services whether they made efforts or failed to make efforts to follow their legal duties and find a way to serve the decision, I can't comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, clearly, they made efforts at least twice, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But they needed to try also the way that is expressly provided in the law. The law expressly provides the procedure when somebody refuses to be served the decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, can a legal system function if citizens simply refuse to receive decisions?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is why the legal system, this is why the law has foreseen such situations and regulated those, expressly and clearly. And there is always a possibility to serve certain decision through the appropriate procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: What if the person continues to refuse despite the procedure?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that this was expressly stated in the law on general administrative procedure. Another attempt is made, the decision is left at the door, the note is taken of the date when the note was or decision was left at the door, and a conclusion is made that the service has been made properly through this procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So once a decision is left at the door, then, then he would be -- at that point you're saying he would be obligated to return the weapon?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The moment of service is indicated in the receipt note respecting the provisions of the law on general administrative procedure that I mentioned. I can't clearly quote them now because I don't have the law in front of me now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to another topic. I'd like to now refer to a video P437, 65 ter 988, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Ms. Dorevska, isn't Minister Boskoski taking responsibility as the person at the very top of the hierarchy in the ministry regarding a matter that took place on the ground? Doesn't he say here that, You know that the minister of the interior never hides away from responsibility and if those who were present at the exercise, that somebody was responsible and I will take that because I am the commander of the Macedonian police, and as minister, I am most accountable. Isn't that what he says?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he did not say he was the commander of the Macedonian police. I believe he said he was in command of Macedonian police. This is an unfortunate incident that took place and I believe that the statement of the minister was given immediately afterwards. I believe that he was emotionally upset at that time and he his idea was to protect people around him, his duty was to do everything to secure the area where the event was taking place.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And how is it that you -- on what basis do you say that he said this or he was emotionally upset at the time and it was his idea to protect the people at the time. On what basis do you say that?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I base this on the fact that we were all witnesses to this through the TV. And very soon after this unfortunate incident where people were killed, the minister gave his statement to the media; and obviously he assumes the entire responsibility personally, although the responsibility perhaps should have been sought elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: But no one was killed in this instance, were they?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were individuals seriously injured.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Okay. And when he says he is in command of the Macedonian police, he is taking responsibility for the police operations on the ground, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that was a drill or something, where the minister, I suppose, stated his wish to participate. And the word "command" in this context I understand exclusively within his legal competences of managing the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: So as the person who is the manager of the Ministry of Interior, he is the highest in the hierarchy of the Ministry of Interior in that chain of command. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, you just said that in the context of using the word "command" it means in the legal context that he was managing the Ministry of Interior. Doesn't that refer to the hierarchy within the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a difference between managing and commanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Well, according to Minister Boskoski, in his view, in his mind, he had the legal competence to command the Macedonian police. Isn't that what he's saying?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat: That was a statement in a perturbed moment, five minutes after an unfortunate incident and the minister was giving a statement to the media. I can't believe you can attach interpretation to each and every word and not in the way that you wish to attach it to now.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Wasn't he then saying that he was in charge of the Macedonian police, as the minister?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Minister is managing the Ministry of Interior. I believe that this is indisputable.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: And as the person -- minister who manages the Ministry of Interior, he is in charge of the ministry, which includes the police, right?

utterances.speaker: VESNA DOREVSKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I take note of the time, and I do have a little bit more to cover and I don't think I can cover it in the next two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What time would you estimate at this point that you will need tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe I should finish within the first session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I thought you said you had a little more to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm trying to be conservative, Your Honour. I'm hoping that I'll finish well before the end of the first session, but I don't wish to mis-estimate the time at this stage. Perhaps 45 minutes to an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn for the evening. We resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 19th day of February, 2008 at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.57 p.m.,
